current_date: July 2022 (cover); in force 'from October 2022' per the council's Planning validation requirements page
current_evidence: The council's Planning validation requirements page (published 01/09/2026) still lists the 13 checklists under 'Planning validation requirements from October 2022', and the separate consultation page says the 2026 lists are drafts (consultation 1-29 September 2026) to be 'finalised and adopted' later, with no adoption date given.

issues.detail: Grokbot's validation list URL points to a consultation draft of the major-applications checklist, not the adopted local list. The 2026 checklists in the /planning-validation/ folder were only out for consultation and have not been adopted. The checklists in force are the July 2022 set (from October 2022) in the /validationpdfs2022/ folder.
issues.evidence: Workbook PDF cover: 'September 2026 DRAFT'. Consultation page: 'the draft local validation lists ... before the updated local validation lists are finalised and adopted' (consultation 1 to 29 September 2026).

issues.detail: The list date 2026-08-01 comes from PDF metadata and does not match the document. The workbook PDF calls itself a September 2026 draft. The adopted list is dated July 2022 and has applied from October 2022.
issues.evidence: Workbook PDF cover 'September 2026 DRAFT'. Adopted major list cover 'July 2022', footer 'Local Requirments List 2022'. Council page heading 'Planning validation requirements from October 2022'.

issues.detail: Grokbot read the 2022 adopted checklists and the 2026 draft checklists side by side (docs_read has both folders) and merged them without saying which is which. Most app_type_rows cite the draft PDFs, so draft triggers are presented as current. For example, Health Impact Assessment is given as 'A desktop Health Impact Assessment is required for Major applications', citing draft Local Plan (2025) Policy DM6. The adopted 2022 list requires an HIA only for development referable to the Mayor. Flood Risk Assessment is given as 'all major developments within Flood Zone 1,2,3a and 3b', but the adopted list requires it in Flood Zone 1 only for sites of 1ha or more.
issues.evidence: Adopted 2022 major list item 23 'Health Impact Assessment - Development referable to the Mayor of London'. Item 21 FRA: 'Sites of 1ha+ in Flood Zone 1; all proposals in Flood Zones 2 or 3 or at surface water flood risk'.

issues.detail: Several local-list items in the major checklist (adopted 2022 version, and repeated in the 2026 draft) have no requirement row. Circular Economy Statement (applications referable to the Mayor). Community Audit (redevelopment of non-residential buildings in community use). Construction Logistics and Environment Management Plan, outline (all applications). Delivery and Servicing Plan, outline (all applications). Materials and Architectural Details (all applications involving operational development). Noise and Vibration Impact Assessment (noise-sensitive uses near noise sources, or noise-generating plant). Parking Design and Management Plan (car, motorcycle or cycle parking proposed). River Impact Study (sites adjoining or near the Ravensbourne, Pool, Thames, Quaggy, Deptford Creek or LLFA ordinary watercourses). Schedule of Accommodation (residential, student or shared living). Site Contamination Assessment (groundworks or works to potentially hazardous buildings; Grokbot has it only under prior approval). Urban Greening Factor Statement (all applications).
Householder: the adopted householder local list requires 'Materials and Architectural Details' for all applications involving operational development. Grokbot has no row for it.
issues.evidence: Adopted 2022 householder checklist local item 10 'Materials and Architectural Details: All applications involving operational development'.

issues.detail: Householder rows include items that are not on the adopted householder list, taken from the draft checklist or from the wrong text: Basement Impact Assessment with trigger 'All applications', Landscaping scheme, Highways/visibility splays, Roof plan and Pre-application advice. The adopted 2022 householder local list has only Archaeology, CIL, FRA form, Heritage Statement, Materials and Architectural Details, Structural Survey and Tree Survey/AMS/AIA/TPP.
issues.evidence: Adopted 2022 householder checklist local items 6 to 12.

issues.detail: Ten of the 12 'Lawful development cert' rows come from checklist 4 (Listed Building Consent / certificate of lawfulness for works to a listed building), not from the LDC existing or proposed checklists (5 and 6). Examples: Design and Access Statement ('For proposals where external works to a listed building are proposed'), Schedule of Works, Structural Survey, Heritage Statement and Street elevations. These apply to listed building works, not to ordinary LDCs.
issues.evidence: Rows cite 4-listed-building-consent-and-certificate-of-lawfulness-for-works-to-a-listed-building.pdf. Separate checklists exist: '5 ... certificate of lawfulness existing' and '6 ... certificate of lawfulness proposed'.

issues.detail: 'Change of use - prior approval' is filled with rows from other prior-notification checklists: larger home extensions (checklist 7: site plan, floor plans, roof plan, photographs), demolition prior notification (checklist 12: contamination, bat survey, HGV routing, method statement) and telecoms (checklist 13). It also has 'Viability Assessment' for loss of a public house, taken from the minor development list. None of these is a change-of-use prior approval checklist. The demolition items should sit under demolition prior notification, but 'Demolition in cons area' is shown as '(none)'.

All 44 Full planning rows are marked 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning'. They combine items from the major and minor checklists without saying which threshold applies. Air Quality Assessment and Health Impact Assessment are major-only, and Circular Economy applies only to Mayor-referable schemes, yet they appear as general Full planning requirements. Outline is shown as '(none)', although the major checklist covers all planning permission applications for major development, including outline.
issues.evidence: Rows note 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning'. Sources are 1-planning-permission-for-major-applications.pdf and 2-planning-permission-for-minor-development.pdf.

issues.detail: Several requirement labels do not match their trigger text. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' under Householder and Full planning has trigger text about an arboricultural method statement and tree protection plan. 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' has retail sequential-test text. 'Block plan / Site plan' under Full planning has BNG/legal agreement text. 'Transport Assessment' has London Plan HC1 heritage text mixed in. 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' under s73 has the trigger 'For amendments which require a deed of variation to a S.106 Agreement', which is the S106 row merged into the ES row.
issues.evidence: Trigger excerpts: 'an arboricultural method statement (AMS) and tree protection plan to BS 5837:2012 are also required.'; 'Environmental Statement (ES) For amendments which require a deed of variation to a S.106 Agreement.'

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are cut-off fragments that do not say when the requirement applies. Examples: Full planning 'Floor plans / Elevations': 'the proposed floor plans. 39.'. 'Environmental Statement': 'subject to EIA but encouraged for'. 'Highways / access details' (Householder, LBC, LDC, Adverts): 'access, landscaping, visibility splays and parking)', which is part of the Design and Access Statement description, not a highways requirement.

The tab items include process text and contact details rather than requirements. Examples: the acknowledgement-letter contact text (Business Support Team 020 8314 7400 / planning@lewisham.gov.uk); 'Duty Planner Service' blurbs (three times); 'If an application is submitted without meeting these requirements ... 21 days' (three times); NPPG advice to seek pre-application advice; 'Providing a Validation Compliance Table will assist officers'. A quote of the Fire Statement height condition is filed under 'Drawing / document standards'.
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Submission rules' entries sourced from the planning-validation-requirements page and the checklists 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8.

issues.detail: The drawing-standard tab items repeat the same text many times because the 2022 and 2026 versions of the same checklists were both extracted. Examples: 'Include a scale bar showing a length of 1metre and 10 metres' appears in roughly 9 entries, and 'be drawn to an identified metric scale' in 5. The NMA and s73 'marked up/annotated amendments' text appears four times.
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Drawing / document standards' (28 entries, from checklists 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 13, in both the 2022 and 2026 versions).

summary: Grokbot's link is to the September 2026 consultation draft of Lewisham's major-applications checklist. The adopted list is still the July 2022 set (in force from October 2022), and Grokbot's list date comes from PDF metadata. The extraction mixes the adopted and draft checklists, misses about a dozen major-list local requirements (CLEMP, Delivery and Servicing Plan, Noise, Urban Greening Factor, River Impact Study and others), and puts listed-building and other prior-notification items under the wrong application types.
